The world has one question for you — seven of them, actually. Once only.
[credLine]
WORLD BACKUPS
Your world is snapshotted automatically before it is ever replaced, plus periodically while you play. Restoring replaces your current world (which is itself backed up first).
NEW WORLD
Two kinds of world. The public one is shared — everyone in it sees each other's builds. A private one is yours alone.
THE WORLD WILL CALL YOU
A name you choose is the one the ledger, the chat, and the dark will use. Skip it and you are Explorer.
SEED (OPTIONAL)
A seed is a world's name: the same seed always builds the same terrain, so typing a friend's seed drops you into their land. Leave it blank to use the shared world.
HOW THIS WAS MADE
A survival sandbox built from scratch — no game engine, no asset files.
THE WORLD
Every hill, cave and coastline is generated by a hand-written WebAssembly kernel. Terrain chunks are greedy-meshed inside wasm and streamed to the GPU with zero copies — vertices upload straight out of linear memory.
THE ENGINE
No Unity, no three.js, no physics library. The WebGL2 renderer, the procedural sky and water, the screen-space ambient occlusion, god rays and bloom are all written for this project — and the render loop allocates nothing per frame.
THE SOUND
Every sound is synthesised at runtime from oscillators and noise. There are no audio files in this build.
THE PEOPLE
Multiplayer runs on a shared websocket world — block edits, chests, dropped items and chat are synchronised, and other players glide smoothly between updates.
AND SOME THINGS
A few systems in here are never explained, and never announced. If you notice them, they were meant for you.
AND YOUR PRIVACY
Your world, your name and everything you build stay on this device — the statistics below are the only thing that leaves it. They are anonymous and aggregate: how many visits reached a world, how long they stayed, how many times a visitor had been here before and how long since their last visit, which kind of device, which systems they found, and which errors stopped them. No names, no accounts, no location, no saved world, nothing that identifies anyone. The totals are readable only by the person who made this — the relay checks a key it keeps privately and returns the report scrambled to anyone else, so not even someone reading this page's source can see them.
AND IF YOU WANT IT TO KEEP GOING
[supportNote]
♥ Support on Ko-fi
One HTML file. Runs in your browser.
Your world saves locally — no sign-up, no account.
THE WORLD ASKS
Seven questions, and no one is watching. There is no name, no account and nothing in the answers that identifies you — they go to the same anonymous totals as the rest, and they are read by the person who built this and nobody else. You can come back and change an answer whenever you like.

USE

PAUSED

How the world runs, how hard it bites, and what sits on your screen.
Day length
How long a full day takes, in real minutes. Shorter days mean more nights.
Difficulty
Peaceful: nothing hunts you. Normal: the world as intended. Hard: more of them, and they hit harder.
Crosshair
The mark at the middle of the screen. Off, a single dot, or a full cross.
Clip replayOn
Keeps the last few seconds of play in memory, so a highlight can be saved with V.
Desktop alertsOff
A system notification for chat and arrivals while the tab is in the background.
World lives onOn
The world keeps ticking while the page is closed, so you return to moved sun, weather and night.
Chat voiceOff
Reads chat messages out loud as they arrive.
VoiceWatcher
Which voice speaks chat and the nightly scripture.
Omen voiceOn
Speaks each night's omen aloud, in the voice above.
Villager voiceOn
The villagers say their lines in their own voices, panned to where they stand.
Resolution
Internal render scale. Lower is faster and softer; Ultra is native and crisp.
Anti-aliasOff
Temporal smoothing that removes edge shimmer when the game renders below your screen's resolution.
Edge smoothing4x
Multisampling: smooths the stair-steps along block edges without blurring textures.
Post FXHigh
Ambient occlusion, bloom and light shafts. Higher looks better and costs more.
LookCinematic
The colour grade: the image as rendered, lightly graded, or cinematic with contrast, haze and grain.
FoliageFull
Draws leaf canopies. Off strips every leaf from the world — a big speedup in forests.
Auto-stepOn
Walk straight up one-block steps. The jump button stays either way. Sneaking never steps.
Battery saverOff
Caps the frame rate at 30, renders at half resolution with no edge smoothing, post FX or shadows over 512, and stops the clip recorder. The phone runs cooler and lasts longer.
Sharp pixelsOff
Renders at the phone's full panel pixels instead of backing off. Crisper on strong phones; the heat guard steps back down on its own if the frame rate slips. Battery saver overrides this.

Throw held:
Press E to close. Break blocks to gather, right-click to place.BAG again to close. Hold the world to gather, PLACE to place.
CRAFTING
Build a Workbench, a Forge, a Lathe — place it and stand beside it, and its recipes unlock here. Each line says which bench it needs; a greyed line tells you why.
TORSO PAINTER
Paint the shirt other players see on your torso. They also see a face, hair, arms and legs — those are drawn for you.
SIGN PAINTER
Paint the sign board — wood shows through unpainted pixels.
SOUNDBOARD
SFX play for nearby players too; phrases are sent to chat.
RADIO
Pick a station — it plays from this boombox for anyone nearby.
CHEST
Click an item to move it between the chest and your pack. A chest is shared — anyone who opens it sees the same contents.
